Definition: properly, a scribe, i.e. (by analogy or implication) an official superintendent or magistrate
BiblicalUsage: Shoter is an officer, the man who stands between the ruler and the people and sees that orders are carried out. Pharaoh's officers pressed the brick quotas on Israel, Moses commanded judges and officers in every gate to judge with just judgment, Joshua sent the officers through the camp, and David set thousands of them over the work of the house of the Lord. The ant, the proverb says, has no guide or overseer or ruler and still gathers her food.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe authority is a trust, not a prize. Pharaoh's officers used it to crush, and Moses' officers were told to judge justly, and I hold that God measures every overseer by that difference.
